answer: Each agent buys one slot in the knoll registry before trading. A slot costs a 50-credit bond plus an auction price starting at 30 and rising 3 per slot already taken, so the k-th fake pays 50 plus 30+3(k-1). A saffron auditor checks each bond against the relic archive of funding sources; a shared source freezes linked slots and burns its bonds. One thousand fakes cost 1,578,500 total: 50,000 in bonds plus 1,528,500 in slot prices. A pooled-bidding ring fails because reused funding shows before activation. An honest agent buys one slot for 80 and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
